## Open Items & Timelines  
| # | Item | Deadline / Status | Update |
|---|------|-------------------|--------|
| 1 | **Integrate MemGPT‑style virtual‑context paging** to offset QA interference at >40 items. | **Start today**; test on 10‑batch simulation (≈50 hrs GPU). | Draft: *“Implement paging layer, log QA accuracy vs. store size.”* |
| 2 | **Rewrite‑vs‑append ablation** with periodic consolidation (arXiv “Consolidation reduces cross‑fact interference”) + MemGPT paging. | **Run within first 3 days of May** (use 1200 GPU‑hrs). | Draft: *“Set up sweep, baseline ‘append‑only’, rewrite‑plus‑consolidation.”* |
| 3 | **Workshop paper (56cc7f88) – coauthor Maya** – outline received, awaiting review. | **Respond by CO‑WRITER due: May 7** | Draft reply: *“Thanks, Maya. The outline looks solid; I’ll add two related benchmark results and circulate by tomorrow.”* |

**Note:**  
- The ICLR rebuttal for submission 4127 has its deadline on day 19 – already past; action is complete.  
- H100 GPU‑quota (2400 hrs/month) is confirmed; schedule experiments on that budget.  

## Experiment Checklist  
- **Baseline:** Naïve append using MemGPT paging; record token budget and QA accuracy per day.  
- **Rewrite:** Structured rewrite + optional consolidation after each day.  
- **Metrics:** F1 gain, QA accuracy curve, token usage, GPU time.  
- **Analysis:** Compare drop‑off beyond 40 items; confirm compression mitigates interference.  

## Overnight Idea  
**Hybrid MemGPT + Consolidation**  
Combining MemGPT virtual paging with the periodic consolidation from the recent arXiv paper should produce a reinforcement of memory compression, keeping the active context succinct while periodically summarizing older facts. This hybrid should both dodge the 9 F1 gap and keep token usage below the 20‑day budget—perfect for the forthcoming workshop and ICLR ablation.
